bug_info.bug_desc: The disable operation was not sequenced as a real operation. In the main control FSM, an accepted disable command transitioned directly from Available to Disabled while op_start_i was still asserted, so the Disabled state treated the pending start as a new invalid request and the operation completed with OpDoneFail. The operation state controller had no disable request handling, so it produced no op_ack/op_update cycle for disable. As a result, the slot-update mux never selected a wipe phase and the internal DPE key slots were not erased. In addition, the only existing wipe-all slot phase was the full-wipe phase tied to wipe_key_o; the disable path needed a distinct internal-only wipe phase so that generated software and hardware keys are preserved when wiping internal key slots.
bug_info.fix_hint: Handle disable as a single-cycle operation in keymgr_dpe_op_state_ctrl: give dis_req_i priority over other requests, add a StDis state that asserts op_ack_o and op_update_o, and return to idle. In keymgr_dpe_ctrl, transition from Available to a new StCtrlDpeDisabling state that keeps op_req asserted until the operation controller acknowledges, then move to StCtrlDpeDisabled. On the disable op_update, select SlotWipeInternalOnly instead of SlotWipeAll, and keep wipe_key_o asserted only for SlotWipeAll so that software/hardware generated keys are not wiped during disablement.
